title: Rotating Cell Culture Systems for Human Cell Culture: Human Trophoblast Cells as a Model
protocol: Weigh out the appropriate amount of Cytodex-3 beads required for the experiment.
Mix 250 mg Cytodex-3 beads with 12 mL Dulbecco phosphate buffered solution (DPBS) in a 50 mL autoclavable conical tube.
Loosely cap the tube and autoclave for 10 min at 110°C.
Remove the conical tube after autoclaving and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Use sterile technique to bring the total volume to 12.5 mL using 1X DPBS.
Cap and store the prepared Cytodex-3 beads at room temperature.
Allow the prepared beads to swell and cool to room temperature prior to use.
Prepare 400 mL of MEM alpha supplemented with sodium bicarbonate, peptone, fructose, galactose, glucose, HEPES, L-glutamine, ITS, and FBS.
Dissolve the required amount of L-15 Leibovitz's powder in tissue-culture grade water to prepare 600 mL of medium.
Mix the prepared MEM alpha solution with the L-15 Leibovitz's medium to achieve a total volume of 1L of RCCS optimized GTSF-2 media.
Filter sterilize the mixed cell culture medium and store at 4°C in the dark.
Add 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin individually to each aliquot of medium used.
Propagate EVTs to ~80% confluency, trypsinize, and count using accepted cell culture practices.
Suspend 1x10^6 EVTs in 4 mL of warmed media.
Gently mix prepared Cytodex-3 beads.
Remove 2.5 mL of prepared beads using a wide tip, sterile serological pipette and transfer to an unused 15 mL conical tube.
Allow the Cytodex-3 beads to settle at the bottom of the tube.
Remove the top layer of DPBS without disturbing the settled Cytodex-3 beads using a pipettor.
Mix 1x106 prepared EVTs in media with the Cytodex-3 beads.
Incubate the cell-bead mixture at room temperature for 30 min, periodically mixing gently.
Incubate the mixture for an additional 30 min at 37°C and 5% CO2, periodically mixing gently.
Remove a 10 mL RCCS from its packaging in a laminar flow cabinet.
Place the RCCS in a sterile 6-well culture plate for stability.
Remove the large stopper from the port of the RCCS.
Bring the total volume of the incubating cell-bead mixture to 10 mL with warmed media.
Load the cell/bead-mixture into the RCCS through the large port, tilting it at a 45° angle (large port up).
Fill the vessel slowly and steadily to avoid positive pressure build-up.
Replace the stopper in the large port of the RCCS after loading is complete.
Remove pistons from two 3-mL syringes and place empty syringes onto small ports.
Add 1-3 mL of media to each syringe.
Slowly open both valves on the RCCS.
Gently replace pistons on syringes attached to small ports.
Add media from one syringe until all bubbles are removed from inside chamber.
Pick up the RCCS and gently tap the side while rotating it to check for bubbles.
If there are any bubbles, rotate the RCCS until the bubbles are under the small port.
Gently push down on the syringe opposite the bubble location to force the bubbles into the port and out of the chamber.
Close one side port.
Gently push down on the other syringe piston to introduce a small amount of positive pressure into the vessel.
Close second valve.
Load the RCCS onto the rotor.
Start the rotation at 19rpm in a 37°C CO2 incubator.
Turn off the rotor and remove the RCCS when changing media.
Pull the pistons up to create some suction, then remove the syringes from each small port.
Place the RCCS on an angle so that the beads settle opposite of the large port.
Open one of the small valves and allow the media to flow out into a waste container.
Remove 2/3 of the media without disturbing the beads or aggregates.
Close the small valve and open the large port.
Add media back into the RCCS through the large port.
Replace the stopper in the large port.
Increase the rotation speed between 0.3-0.7 rpm after each feeding once the aggregates start growing visibly.
Remove the RCCS from the rotor.
Remove syringes from each small port and place the RCCS on an angle so that beads settle opposite of the large port.
Open one of the small valves to allow media to flow out into a waste container.
Remove 1/3 of the media in this manner.
Close the small valve and open the large port.
Gently swirl the vessel to disperse aggregates back into solution.
Empty liquid mixture into a sterile 50ml conical tube.
Allow collected aggregates to settle in the conical tube before using supernatant to thoroughly wash the culture vessel.
Maximize recovery of aggregates for downstream assays immediately.
